payload.entry: url-identity baseline: at ae3a432b dedupe_key_for appended url.path() verbatim, so the Medium @edominguez.se and %40edominguez.se spellings produced two identity keys; ref find missed the twin and capture dedupe allowed double capture. New clip_url test failed pre-fix with left "https://medium.com/@..." vs right "https://medium.com/%40..." (authentic failure observed).

url-identity fix: normalize_path_escapes in src/native/highlights_ref/clip_url.rs used by dedupe_key_for. Decodes RFC 3986 unreserved bytes plus explicit @ (the verified Medium twin); retains all other escapes with uppercase hex; single left-to-right pass so %2540 never collapses to @; malformed % sequences pass through. Trim of trailing slash happens before normalization so retained %2F is never treated as a separator. Stored source_url/cleaned output unchanged; all consumers (ref find query+stored keys, sources check_dedupe/legacy_hits, collection overlap, capture routing intent) share the key so one fix covers lookup, duplicate detection, and collections.

url-identity tests: 6 new regression tests pass -- clip_url key normalization (Medium twin, unreserved decode, hex-case agreement, non-ASCII) + delimiter-distinctness (encoded / ? # % stay distinct, no recursive decode, malformed passthrough); ref_library stored_identity/url_query_keys twin test; sources check_dedupe twin refusal; collection check_collection_overlap twin test; CLI bob ref find test with both twin notes asserting both queries return both notes with duplicate_identity. Focused suites: 802 lib tests (highlights_ref+ref_library+url_routing) ok; gate clippy (just check flags) clean; cargo fmt clean.
